Messages.Author: Herve Guillemet
Messages.Body:
1) One of your vampire carries the Blood Tears. An opposing vampire wants
to play another Blood Tears. Can you burn your Blood Tears and gain 2
blood before the contest begins ?

2) Can you play a 2nd tradition and untap a prince when the action
does not have stealth.

3) Can you play a 2nd tradition to play a reaction like Telepatic
misdirection ?

4) When you play additional strikes with Silence of Death, does the opposing
vampire get to strike before the additional strikes ?

Thanks,

== Herve Guillemet

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
guil...@marsouin.imed.jussieu.fr (Herve Guillemet) writes:

>1) One of your vampire carries the Blood Tears. An opposing vampire wants
>to play another Blood Tears. Can you burn your Blood Tears and gain 2
>blood before the contest begins ?

Answer still pending, sorry.

>2) Can you play a 2nd tradition and untap a prince when the action
>does not have stealth.

No. You can never play a reaction card which gives intercept unless
you need intercept.

>3) Can you play a 2nd tradition to play a reaction like Telepatic
>misdirection ?

No. Card text says that the Prince/Justicar must attempt to block.
If the block fails, you could then play another Reaction card with
the newly untapped Prince/Justicar, of course.
(Any time you gain intercept, you are attempting to block. By definition
you don't need intercept unless you are attempting to block, and you
can't gain intercept you don't need, so...)

>4) When you play additional strikes with Silence of Death, does the opposing
>vampire get to strike before the additional strikes ?

Yes. Each "announce strike - resolve strike" set resolves in unison
with the opposing minion. The "resolve strike" steps may be staggered
if only one minion has struke with First Strike, and subsequent
"announce" steps (with their matching resolve steps) may have to be
skipped by a minion who doesn't have additional strikes.

See the rules outline for a complete breakdown of the entire combat
process. (Posted here every month, and available from my VtES page:
http://www.HomeFree.Net/view/page.exe?236

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
Herve Guillemet (guil...@marsouin.imed.jussieu.fr) wrote:
: 1) One of your vampire carries the Blood Tears. An opposing vampire wants

: to play another Blood Tears. Can you burn your Blood Tears and gain 2
: blood before the contest begins ?

My guess is that as long as you do so before his/her equipping action is
completed, then that should not be a problem. It doesn't start contesting
until it is in play, and you can burn yours whenever you want as long as
it is not contested and is in play... at least, that's how I read the card.

: 2) Can you play a 2nd tradition and untap a prince when the action
: does not have stealth.

: 3) Can you play a 2nd tradition to play a reaction like Telepatic
: misdirection ?

: 4) When you play additional strikes with Silence of Death, does the opposing

: vampire get to strike before the additional strikes ?

??

I thought the card text was (from the spoiler list):

Silence of Death (Combat) 1 Blood/Quietus
Only usable before range is chosen. This vampire gets First Strike with
hand and melee weapon strikes for the remainder of the round.
Superior: As above, and this vampire gets an optional manuever during
this round of combat.
Illus. Stuart Beel

If I understand your questions correctly, you have played Silence of Death
and are now going to play some additional strikes afterwards. If so, then
yes, they get their normal strike before the additional strikes begin. The
phases go like this:

Choose Strikes
Resolve First Strikes completely.
Resolve Normal Strikes completely.
Choose Additional Strikes
Resolve First Strike Additional Strikes completely.
Resolve Normal First Strike Additional Strikes completely.
etc.

See either the rule book or one of the rules references to see that normal
strikes are definitely resolved before additional strikes begin, regardless
of whether any of the "additional" strikes are first strikes.

The first strike specification simply denotes that a given strike is resolved
before a normal strike chosen at the same time.

-James

This relates to the Heidleburg issue.
During an action you can only do relavant things such as react.
Before the action is announced or after it is complete you may do
things but not in the middle of an action.
Personally I feel you should only do things on your turn (Like giving
up the edge except for a vote, or yielding) but I have no support for
that position and its just my sense of asthetics.
To allow things to be done in the middle of an action muddies up the
game and brings up timing issues like other games have.
Keep it simple.
Rory

As far as keeping it simple goes: "Anytime *between actions* during any
Meth's minion phase and/or during any other phase" should eliminate all
timing concerns. Further restriction to "on one's own turn" would just
be a matter of preference, with no further simplicity gained.

I'm all for the former, but against the latter.

If Rory or you (Corrupter) would care to formally submit the house rule,
I'll be happy to include it (as always). If not, I'll probably include
my version anyhow (I'm not prone to adding all of the variations posted
here willy-nilly - not enough time in the day, you know).
